messages:
rhea (AE): Heads-up: Prospect wants to move 100% of their inference from CompetitorX to Redwood. They ran a small smoke and flagged two blockers: token count variance causing billing mismatch, and a missing response header field their pipeline expects. They want a 30-day technical POC + pricing for a pilot.

neil (SE): Do we have a concrete example of the header and a sample payload? that helps us decide shim vs product fix.

rhea (AE): They pasted:
`POST /v1/chat`
`{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Extract action items from meeting notes..."}], "max_tokens":500}`
CompetitorX billed 24,600 tokens for batch of 100 calls; Redwood shows 24,000.

arpit (Eng): Likely tokenizer differences + CompetitorX auto-appends metadata to `X-Orig-Response` header. Two approaches: add compatibility proxy to map headers and surface competitor token counts, or normalize tokens on our side and return `x-normalized-tokens`. Proxy approach is non-invasive for POC.

sam (SRE): For network/ops: if they want semi-dedicated capacity, we'll need test CIDRs and expected peak RPS. Also, if they require customer-managed KMS, tell them provisioning takes a few days.

rhea (AE): They can give us test IPs and will use Okta SAML SSO. Also asked if we support bringing their KMS keys (yes).

sec-bot: Security note: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS + GCP CMEK) and provide an onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/sec/onboard. For SAML, we need SP metadata and a test account. If they request bespoke logs retention, file a ticket.

neil (SE): I'll run a tokenization comparator: same inputs through CompetitorX tokenizer (they shared an example dump) vs our tokenizer and log per-token diffs. I'll include cases with special unicode, long-form templates, and stop sequences.

arpit (Eng): For the response header, quick proxy patch to rewrite `X-CX-Metadata` -> `X-RW-Metadata` is a 1hr job. For token billing normalization: we can add `normalized_token_count` to responses during the POC only. That gives them a drop-in field so their billing reconciliation can use our number.

tara (Sales Eng): Pricing for 30-day pilot: two options. 1) Hosted pilot with $10k usage credit + engineering support. 2) Short Dedicated trial: $8k/week reserved nodes (min 4 weeks) + tech onboarding. Need expected token/day to recommend. rhea, ask them to fill the pilot sizing quick-sheet.

rhea (AE): They estimate 40 RPS peak, avg 900 tokens per call, rough 95M tokens for 30 days.

tara (Sales Eng): Ok with numbers: hosted+credit makes sense; Dedicated looks expensive for 30 days. I'll draft a conservative cost scenario and send.

neil (SE): I'll post an initial token-diff report in this thread by EOD tomorrow, plus a small acceptance test (10 prompts) that they can run locally to verify parity.

arpit (Eng): Note: CompetitorX has a default behavior of trimming trailing whitespace before tokenization; our tokenizer keeps it. That alone explains a ~2-3% delta in some cases. Suggest either strip whitespace in the proxy or adjust downstream billing.

legal-team: If pilot requires NDA amendment or altered SLAs, loop us in. We'll also provide DPA/SOC2 copies.

rhea (AE): Prospect also asked about how we handle model rollbacks for parity (they want deterministic versions). We support pinning model versions; we can guarantee the exact model hash during the pilot.

sam (SRE): Operational checklist for pilot: 1) whitelist CIDR; 2) provide SAML metadata + test user; 3) provide KMS ARN if using CMEK; 4) expected warmup window and peak schedule. We'll provision logs buckets and short-term retention.

neil (SE): Deliverables: tokenization delta report, 10-case parity test suite, header mapping shim PR, normalization field proposal, and sample reconciliation doc. I'll link artifacts here.

rhea (AE): I'll coordinate with the customer to send items and confirm timeline. Thanks team.

sec-bot: Reminder: KMS bring-your-own requires key access review, estimate 2-3 business days.

tara (Sales Eng): I'll attach the cost scenarios in a follow-up.

arpit (Eng): One more thought: if their pipeline checks exact JSON structure in responses, we should ask for a sample validator or schema so we can ensure parity or add a transformer.

rhea (AE): Good call — I'll request a validator and their smoke harness.

neil (SE): Great. I'll start the comparator now and post results in this thread.
